latest_final: After an earlier mugging, the company president avoided carrying large sums, but when kidnappers demanded a ransom of more than one million yen for a family member, he had to take money to the handoff. He feared that an exact total of one million yen would signal to the kidnappers that he had not brought the money they expected, so he added genuine cash to make the actual amount harder to identify. He also padded some bundles with paper and placed separate bundles of real cash on top, hoping the kidnappers would see genuine money first rather than quickly detect that the bag was short of the demanded ransom. The answers establish that the exact one-million-yen figure carried this significance, but not precisely why.
